keyFindings.description: The root index row this pull request adds still gives the Python runner form as `uvx <name>@<version>` — the exact form rounds 2 and 3 established is wrong by default, and the one the page it points at now spends twenty lines refuting (`tools.md:95` gives `uvx --from <package>@<version> <command>` as the general form; `tools.md:193-201` carries the `uvx pyyaml@6.0.2` transcript that shows the short form resolving the typed token as the PyPI project). AGENTS.md is auto-loaded into every session started in this repository, Legion's own phase workers included, so this is the highest-reach copy of the three and the one a role meets before it ever opens the skill. The round-2 correction landed in two copies of three and missed this one (`jj diff --from afb6d6884054 --to 818e52c01c0e --summary` and `--from 818e52c01c0e --to 1ca563330ac5 --summary` both omit AGENTS.md). The row is internally inconsistent too: its `bunx --package <name>@<version> <binary>` and `go run <module>@<version>` entries are the coordinate-bearing forms and `uvx` is the only one that is not.

'the same line next time gets the same bytes whether the cache was warm or cold' is false for two of the three runners, and it is the premise of the test the page tells a worker to apply to new cases (`tools.md:66-69`). Driven here on the page's own example with an empty UV_CACHE_DIR: `uvx -v --from httpie@3.2.4 http --version` printed 'Resolved 16 packages in 599ms' and selected `requests==2.34.2`, `urllib3==2.8.0`, `certifi==2026.10.23` as '[compatible]' from ranges. The coordinate and version pin one distribution; the rest of the closure is resolved against the live index at run time, so a cold run after any upstream release installs different bytes. The same holds for `bunx`. `go run <module>@<version>` is the one form where the claim is true, through MVS over the module's own go.mod plus go.sum and sum.golang.org, which the page cites only as pinning 'a version's bytes'. A worker told a pinned uvx line is byte-stable will cite such a run as reproducible evidence in a handoff and will treat the transitive closure as pinned when it is not. Same text at docs/kubernetes.md:202-204 and in the committed bundle. Related, one clause away: the stated test ('after your command exits, does anything else resolve differently?') returns 'withheld' for the page's own sanctioned example at `tools.md:82-85`, whose justification is that the runtime keeps `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR` and the workspace on the issue's volume so a later pod reuses it — a `.venv` or `node_modules` there is exactly what every later command in that workspace resolves through. The three-artefact derivation above it is sound; it is the one-line test offered for new cases that does not reproduce its own answers.

The provenance passage added to replace round 2's spoofable `npm view` check repeats that defect in a new form: 'npm verifies a provenance attestation when it is published, so it is the one part of an entry a publisher cannot forge by writing a string' and 'Present for the project, empty for the squatter'. An npm provenance attestation binds an artifact to the repository and workflow that built it; an attacker publishing a squat from a public GitHub Actions workflow in their own repository gets a genuine, registry-verified attestation. The page never tells the reader to read the attestation's subject repository, so the only discriminator it offers is again generalised from the one squatter that happens to publish none. Same text at docs/kubernetes.md:258-270. The binding rule above it (the coordinate comes from the project's own published installation instructions, reached independently of the registry) is correct and is what keeps this at one clause: an attestation corroborates only when its subject repository is read and is the project's; presence alone says nothing about identity.

'Your container is an unprivileged user with no writable system prefix: `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt` and `/home` are read-only' (same at docs/kubernetes.md:160-162). Measured in a live role container: `/home` is `drwxr-xr-x root root` and refuses a write, but `$HOME` is `/home/legion`, `drwx------ legion legion`, and a write there succeeds. A reader planning where a per-issue install lands reads this as 'my home is read-only', which is false, in a page whose whole subject is what a role can and cannot do for itself. The tester has carried this as a standing note since round 1 and the architect asked for it as a finding. One clause: `/home` itself is root's; your own `$HOME` is writable, and what rules out installing there is the ruling the next section draws, not the filesystem.

The supersession note gives `shellcheck` its route and leaves the item's fifth tool, PyYAML, with none. Item 5 recorded jq, ssh, ssh-keygen, shellcheck and PyYAML with a `$HOME/.local` route for each; the note withdraws that route for all of them, resolves the first four, and sends 'anything the image lacks' to tools.md, whose three forms are all command runners. So a Python library for an ad-hoc script now has no documented route, and `tools.md:218-229` tells the worker that a thing no runner reaches is an image change to escalate to the architect. Measured in a role container: `python3 -c 'import yaml'` is ModuleNotFoundError; `uv run --with pyyaml==6.0.2 --no-project python -c 'import yaml'` works in under a second. This is the same defect round 2 raised about shellcheck, fixed for shellcheck and left for the library case: a working documented step replaced by an escalation. One bullet — name the library form beside shellcheck's, or add it to tools.md's runner list.

threads: All fifteen threads — the eight of round 1 and the seven of round 2 — now carry the implementer's disposition and are resolved by it, which is the discipline the first two rounds lacked. I read every resolution against the tree and accept all fifteen; none is unresolved and I unresolved none. The five findings of this round are new threads.
verifiedMyself: uvx's resolution of a pinned run, with an empty UV_CACHE_DIR: `uvx -v --from httpie@3.2.4 http --version` → 'Resolved 16 packages in 599ms', selecting requests==2.34.2, urllib3==2.8.0, certifi==2026.10.23 as [compatible]; the plain run prints 3.2.4.
The new runner claims: `uvx --from shellcheck-py@0.10.0.1 shellcheck --version` → 'ShellCheck - shell script analysis tool' / 'version: 0.10.0'; `uvx --from httpie@3.2.4 http --version` → 3.2.4.

The attestation transcripts: `npm view @biomejs/biome dist.attestations` returns the SLSA provenance object the document quotes and `npm view biome dist.attestations` is empty; ruff 0.14.0's PyPI JSON carries `provenance` on none of its 19 files.

The code citations of the new section: UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR and UV_CACHE_DIR at packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/podkind.go:194-195; GOCACHE, GOMODCACHE and BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR at manifest.go:735-737; installBlock's `/usr/bin/flock … bun add` at plugins.go:225.
The /home claim: /home is drwxr-xr-x root root and refuses a touch; $HOME=/home/legion is drwx------ legion legion and accepts one.
PyYAML's absence and its uv route: `python3 -c 'import yaml'` → ModuleNotFoundError; `uv run --with pyyaml==6.0.2 --no-project python -c 'import yaml'` → works.
acceptedThisRound: The uvx coordinate rewrite: `uvx --from <package>@<version> <command>` as the general Python form, the short form kept only where the project's name is its command's and checked.

The coordinate rule's new ground: identity comes from the project's own published installation instructions reached independently of the registry, with npm view demoted to publisher-written corroboration.
The withheld-capability section, derived from three artefacts of this repository rather than from a reading of the ruling; every one of its code citations checks out.
Both surviving copies of the 'cannot fetch it for itself' overstatement, in docs/kubernetes.md:155 and on the published site.
The size paragraph's 'not a slice of that 22-layer figure' re-anchoring, and the LEGION-748 note's `**Superseded 2026-10-24 (INFRA-221):**` lead with shellcheck's measured route.
